newsitem.title: USA: Lehman denies U.S. bond index miscalculation rumor.
newsitem.headline: Lehman denies U.S. bond index miscalculation rumor.

text.p: Lehman Bros on Monday denied a rumor circulating in the U.S. Treasury market regarding a miscalculation of its main bond index.
"I am unaware of any mistake; I heard nothing from investors," said Jack Malvey, chief fixed income strategist at Lehman, who is responsible for Lehman's 15 separate bond indices.
He acknowledged that there have been times when minor adjustments have been made, but those were mainly in the newer indices.

Earlier on Monday, bond traders said a miscalculation by Lehman forced investors to overextend their durations late last week, only to unwind those extensions Monday. That was cited as contributing to the day's Treasuries selloff.
Malvey said the confusion could have come from Friday's report that durations were 4.50 years at the end of July, a touch below Lehman's forecast from July 28 of 4.51 years.
He added that there was no surprise, since it alerted investors last Monday that durations had fallen to 4.46 on July 25 from 4.62 years at the end of June.
The decline was due to a shortening of the mortgage index on the surge in prepayments, Malvey said.
